title: Puccini Cucumber (Puccini F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Puccini cucumber is an F1 hybrid (pickling type) cucumber variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Puccini cucumber is an F1 hybrid (pickling type) cucumber variety, also sold or known as Puccini F1 or Puccini pickling cucumber. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Rijk Zwaan (distributed by Allied Botanical).

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Puccini F1 or Puccini pickling cucumber, this is the same cucumber. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [cucumber variety finder](/crop-varieties/cucumber), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first picking 25 to 38 days after sowing, then every other day. Yield, by the seller's count: 24 to 30 t/ha at pickling size, about 1.5 kg per vine (Allied technologist's figure). No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cucumber fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [damping off](/diseases/damping-off), [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First picking 25 to 38 days after sowing, then every other day.
**Yield:** 24 to 30 t/ha at pickling size, about 1.5 kg per vine (Allied technologist's figure).
**Fruit:** Short and squat gherkin type picked at about 7 to 12 cm, thin bumpy skin, dark green at the stem end fading to light green.
**Season:** Dry season (March sowing after onion in Nueva Ecija).
Short internodes, up to three fruits per node.
Grown in the open after onion in Nueva Ecija, on the onion crop's leftover fertility.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the pickling cucumber grown under contract by more than 300 Nueva Ecija farmers on about 80 ha for a Unilever dressing supply chain, after Allied Botanical brought it to Bataan and Talavera growers from 2012. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Puccini cucumber

Cucumber gives its first fruit fast, often in five to six weeks. Pick a variety bred to tolerate downy mildew if you plant near the rains. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is Puccini F1 the same as Puccini?
items.a: Yes. Puccini F1 is another name for Puccini. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Puccini?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
